title: Apply for a beekeeper registration
summary: Learn how to register as a beekeeper if you plan to keep honey bee hives in NSW.
intro: If you want to keep one or more hives of honey bees in NSW, you’ll need to be registered as a beekeeper with NSW Department of Primary Industries (DPI).
who_can_apply: Must keep one or more hives of honey bees in NSW.
what_you_need: A Department of Primary Industries username and password
Details of the number of hives and their location

how_to_steps.text: Select the 'Apply online' button. You'll be taken to the DPI Biosecurity and Food Safety (BFS) portal.
Sign up or create a login.

more_info.text: Bee registration issued under the Biosecurity Act 2015 will be valid for 2 years.
The fee depends on your registration type:

All NSW beekeepers will need to adhere to the Australian Honey Bee Industry Biosecurity Code of Practice as a condition of registration. For more information, visit the Department of Primary Industries website.

faqs.q: Who needs to register as a beekeeper?
faqs.a: Anyone who wants to keep one or more hives of honey bees in NSW.

faqs.q: Where do I apply for beekeeper registration?
faqs.a: You must apply through the NSW Department of Primary Industries (DPI).

faqs.q: What do I need to apply for beekeeper registration?
faqs.a: You will need a DPI username and password, your business and concession details (if applicable), details of the number and location of hives, and payment.
